---
title: "Data viz"
---

Eight categorical chart colours, drawn from the crew, ordered so the
first colours seen are also the most legible against the active
ground. The palette ships in two variants (light + dark) and the
active set is exported as CSS custom properties on `:root`.

## Slot table

| Slot | Light hex | Dark hex | Crew |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--pequod-chart-1` | `#0D2F42` | `#EAE1D7` | log-800 / log-100 (deep ink ↔ warm paper) |
| `--pequod-chart-2` | `#0082B1` | `#A6DFFF` | Starbuck |
| `--pequod-chart-3` | `#A83732` | `#E3877C` | Ahab |
| `--pequod-chart-4` | `#177C55` | `#82C4A2` | Tashtego |
| `--pequod-chart-5` | `#CA6435` | `#FFD9BB` | Stubb |
| `--pequod-chart-6` | `#253E82` | `#838CCF` | Queequeg |
| `--pequod-chart-7` | `#6A4A00` | `#DEC577` | Pip |
| `--pequod-chart-8` | `#552823` | `#A17069` | Daggoo |

The first slot is anchored to the strongest body-text contrast in each
mode — use it for the primary series and reach for slots 2..N in
order for additional series. Charts with two series should use
slots 1 + 2 (paper-vs-Starbuck), three series should add slot 3
(Ahab), and so on.

## Read the active set from JS

```js
const root = document.documentElement;
const series = Array.from({ length: 8 }, (_, i) =>
  getComputedStyle(root).getPropertyValue(`--pequod-chart-${i + 1}`).trim()
);
```

The values flip automatically when the user toggles light / dark
because the dark stylesheet redeclares the same custom properties
under its own `:root`. Charts that pull from `getComputedStyle` at
each render pick the new palette up without rerunning the layout
pipeline.

## Read from an Observable cell

```js
// Pull all eight slots into an array Observable can use as a scale.
const pequod = Array.from({ length: 8 }, (_, i) =>
  getComputedStyle(document.documentElement)
    .getPropertyValue(`--pequod-chart-${i + 1}`)
    .trim()
);

Plot.plot({
  marks: [
    Plot.barY(data, { x: "category", y: "value", fill: "category" })
  ],
  color: { range: pequod }
})
```

## Read from R (knitr `results: asis`)

Inject the active slot values into an R chunk via Quarto's HTML
post-processing:

```r
# In a chunk that runs in the browser session (e.g. via reactable
# or DT with a custom render hook), the same getComputedStyle call
# applies. Server-side R cannot read CSS custom properties because
# no DOM exists; for static R plots, hardcode the hex values from
# the table above or read them from a YAML config you keep in sync
# with _pequod-palette.scss.
```

## Restraint

The eight slots are deliberate. Six of them carry strong crew
identity; the seventh (Pip) is a warm dark yellow that doesn't read
well as a primary series colour on the dark variant; the eighth
(Daggoo) is a deep brown. Don't paint every series — most charts
only need two or three slots. The point of a constrained palette is
that the first colour a reader sees is always institutional.
